page: Vultr vx1-m-48c-384g-2880s is a memory-optimized server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 48 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 24 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and SHA_NI. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 2880 GB NVMe SSD, delivering high-speed local read and write capabilities. The server configuration also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no dedicated GPUs on this instance, meaning all workloads rely entirely on the AMD EPYC CPU resources.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier performance, ranking in the top 10% for Geekbench single-core and multi-core metrics, as well as stress-ng single-core CPU performance. Its memory subsystem is highly efficient, with large-block read and write memory bandwidth tests scoring in the top 10%. Multi-core stress-ng performance, Passmark CPU scores, and Redis SET operations, which achieve 85.37 million operations per second, all rank in the top 25%. For LLM inference, the server achieves strong performance on text generation with medium-sized 7B models, though performance drops to average levels on larger 70B models.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and substantial local NVMe storage, this server offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive and database workloads that do not require GPU acceleration. The combination of 384.0 GB of RAM and 2880 GB of fast NVMe storage makes it highly suitable for hosting large relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, data analytics pipelines, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
